_doc: Severity policy for Bearer findings in small internal employee tools (IDV: CLI scripts, Excel/CSV processing, file tooling, small dashboards).
Bearer's defaults assume a web application with untrusted users - several rules then fire on completely normal script code (e.g. open(path) with a function argument).
Applied to tool == 'bearer' only, never to categories secret/malware/malicious-package/unscannable.
'reason' is German on purpose: gvintra shows it to employees next to the downgraded finding.
Rules are checked top to bottom, the FIRST matching 'match' (fnmatch glob on the Bearer rule id) wins. Rules not listed keep Bearer's severity.
mode 'set' = replace severity, mode 'min' = raise to at least this severity (never lowers).
Blocking in gvintra: critical/high/medium block (high/medium can be justified per finding), low/info are hints only.
Disable for comparison: --no-severity-policy or UNIFIED_SCAN_SEVERITY_POLICY=off. Other file: UNIFIED_SCAN_SEVERITY_POLICY_FILE=/path.json

'base_image': CVEs found by trivy-image in the base image of a Dockerfile (OS packages of e.g. python:3.x-slim, not the uploaded code) become 'severity' (a hint). Exception with keep_critical_with_fix: a critical CVE that already has a fixed version keeps blocking - rebuilding the image fixes it.
Line check in unified_scan.py (not configurable here): a critical *_code_injection finding whose source line only calls setattr/getattr/delattr (no eval/exec/compile) is lowered to high.
Rules may name a 'tool' (default 'bearer'); only 'bearer' and 'checkov' findings are re-rated by 'rules'.

'guarddog': a GuardDog finding on a package within the top 'trusted_top_n' of the registry's download ranking (GuardDog's own top_<ecosystem>_packages.json) becomes 'severity'. Its source-code heuristics fire constantly on big popular packages; typosquats are not on the list and keep blocking.
